question.text: This fourth dynasty pharaoh is best known for building the only surviving great wonder of the world, the Great Pyramid of Giza.
question.clue: Flinders Petrie discovered the only three-dimensional depiction of this ruler, a small ivory statuette.

swap.text: This Egyptian pharaoh and husband of Nefertiti began the worship of the sun disk, which may be why records of him were erased after his reign.
swap.clue: This man wrote a "Great Hymn" to his namesake and was possibly succeeded by Smenkhkare.

question.leadin: This ruler's capital at Amarna was discovered by Flinders Petrie, and his wife was Nefertiti.
question.text: Name this 18th dynasty pharaoh who attempted to establish monotheistic sun worship.
question.clue: Like his father, who married a non-royal woman named Tiy, he married a woman who was not of royal blood, the daughter of a vizier named Ay.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about famous archaeological finds in Egypt.
swap.text: The 1799 discovery of this large fragment of a black stele [stee-lee] allowed scholars to understand hieroglyphs, since it included Greek, Demotic, and heiroglphyic translations of a law.
swap.clue: That rediscovery occurred in 1799 while the French soldier Pierre-Francois Bouchard was on the Napoleonic campaign in Egypt.

question.text: Roman Emperor Hadrian had one of these buildings named for him built on the Acropolis. Nineveh once was the home of one of these buildings named for the Assyrian king Ashurbanipal [ash-oor-BAN-uh-pawl].
question.clue: The Baghdad House of Wisdom was originally founded as a private one of these institutions.

swap.text: Cleopatra was the last ruler of this Hellenistic dynasty which was founded by its namesake satrap in 305 BC and ruled Egypt until it was conquered by the Romans in 30 BC.
swap.clue: It supplied several of the ships destroyed by Agrippa at Actium, and it was an ally of Mark Antony.

question.leadin: Name these Pharaohs from the Egyptian 18th Dynasty.
question.text: This pharaoh sent expeditions to Puntland in modern-day Somalia. She was succeeded by Thutmose III, during whose reign several historical records had this female pharaoh's image wiped from them.
question.clue: This ruler's mortuary temple at Deir el-Bahari includes a relief detailing a trading expedition to the Land of Punt, which brought back incense and myrrh trees.

swap.leadin: Name some military leaders of the ancient Near East FTPE.
swap.text: A man by this name founded a kingdom in Egypt after Alexander's death. Many rulers sharing this name ruled Egypt for centuries afterwards.
swap.clue: A figure with this name explained the apparent motion of the planets using "epicycles" in the Almagest.

question.leadin: During a procession honoring this event, Fatimid caliphs would anoint a structure on Roda Island.
question.text: Name this recurring event. The periods of Peret and Shemu followed this event, which, according to an ancient calendar, occurred during the time of Akhet.
question.answerHtml: flooding of the Nile River [accepting equivalents for “flooding” like inundation; prompt on flooding with “Of what body of water?”] (The device is the Nilometer.)

swap.leadin: Note to moderator: read the answerline to the third part carefully. Constantine II moved an obelisk from this site to the center of the Circus Maximus, where Augustus had placed one from Heliopolis 300 years earlier.
swap.text: Name this temple complex in Luxor. Priests based at this temple's Great Hypostyle Hall likely destroyed reliefs created by Akhenaten, who sidelined and replaced them with worship of Aten.

question.text: In a Middle Kingdom "tale" titled for this profession, a serpent recounts how a flaming star killed 74 members of his kin. That serpent, who is the Lord of Punt, discusses bravery with a member of this profession.
question.answerHtml: sailor [or al-Baḥriyy; accept The Story of the Shipwrecked Sailor; prompt on merchant]

swap.leadin: Name these Wonders of the Ancient World.
swap.text: Ptolemy I Soter had this structure built by the architect Sostratos on the island of Pharos.
swap.clue: Statues of Arsinoe, along with other parts of this building, were discovered underwater in 1994 by Jean Yves Empereur.

question.leadin: Answer the following about Egypt's Hellenistic period.
question.text: During the Hellenistic age, Egypt was ruled by a dynasty founded by this leader, one of the Macedonian generals who had conquered the Persian Empire.
question.clue: He acquired his first wife Artacama during the mass wedding at Susa, cemented a later alliance by marrying Antipater's daughter Eurydice, and finally chose another wife, Berenice, to elevate to the title of queen.

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about cities of ancient Egypt.
swap.text: This first capital of ancient Egypt is still unexcavated due to the obscurity of its exact location along the Nile River, but literary references to it abound in ancient texts. The eponymous confederacy that united Egypt under Menes was located here.

question.leadin: Lake Moeris was created by a canal to this area that made it viable for agricultural production.
question.text: Three pharaohs named Senusret created a massive hydraulic system to export water from what area, which also names a group of encaustic funerary portraits from Ptolemaic Egypt?
question.answerHtml: Fayūm [accept Fayum Oasis, prompt on Western Desert or Libyan Desert]

swap.leadin: Herodotus claimed the thickness of Egyptian skulls at this battle was explained by not wearing turbans, and noted that Polycrates of Samos sent forty warships of unreliable scoundrels to take part.
swap.text: Name this 525 BC battle in which the Egyptian Psamtik III fell after the Greek general Phanes directed the Persians to some Arabs who helped them cross the Sinai desert.

question.leadin: Although his name does not appear on the Turin King List, most scholars dispute Manetho's claim that this pharaoh ruled for 66 years.
question.text: Name this Old Kingdom pharaoh. A causeway links the Great Sphinx constructed by this man to his pyramid, which he literally named after his own greatness.
question.clue: This son of Khufu succeeded his half-brother Djedefre and, much like Khufu and Menkaure, he built his own great pyramid at Giza. According to Manetho and Herodotus, he ruled for 66 years and may have also built the Sphinx.

swap.text: Little is known about him except for his Great Pyramid and the five boats buried next to it.
swap.clue: This pharaoh whose reign saw the construction of the first and largest pyramid at Giza.

question.leadin: Identify the following about monumental columns.
question.text: Constructed of red Aswan granite, this Corinthian column, which despite its name was actually constructed by Diocletian to commemorate his defeat of the Alexandrian revolt, stands atop the former ground of the Serapeum.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the end of the Old Kingdom, FTPE.
swap.text: Toward the very end of the Old Kingdom, the Pyramid Texts began to be replaced by these religious texts, as exemplified by discoveries at the Balat necropolis. In general, they made the afterlife more accessible to commoners than the Pyramid Texts.
